message:
test(host): measure the worst case instead of reasoning about it

Test 2. No product change. The reviewer asked for the injected path to report what a kill
confirmation actually costs, and it could not, because the injection was cheating.

The fault kill returned false immediately. That reached the lingering branch, which is what it was
for, but it reported a 3us teardown -- a number that measured nothing. A kill that is never
confirmed does not return instantly; it costs the whole of kKillConfirmMs. So the injection now
spends that window before reporting failure, which is what the real call would do.

With that, the worst case stops being arithmetic. The header has been claiming that a call which
times out and then meets a helper that will not die takes about six seconds rather than one,
because the deadline bounds the WAIT and the confirmation is a second budget on top. Measured at a
400ms deadline, twice: spawn 102ms, wait 399-400ms, teardown 5001ms, total 5503ms. At the product's
one second deadline the same arithmetic lands near six, which is what the comment says.

Two checks now hold it: the teardown really does spend the confirmation window, and the total
exceeds it -- so anyone who later writes "one second" as a bound on the call fails a test rather
than misleading a reader.

This is the second time on this path that I reported a number I had not measured. The first was
"kill confirmation is about 166ms", which was a subtraction that also contained the spawn. Both
came from describing a stage instead of timing it.

15 checks, two runs, 5503ms both times. Still starts one sleeping copy of itself and nothing else.
